lines.text: This is Mauna Loa in 2022, the largest active volcano in the world.
At one fissure, the lava fountains stood twenty to twenty-five metres high.
In about two weeks, it put out around a hundred and forty-five million cubic metres of lava and ash.
On the official scale of volcanic eruptions, all of that rates a zero.
Now Redoubt, in Alaska, in 2009. About twenty million cubic metres, by a different measure. It rated a three.
So what is this scale actually measuring? The full video opens on it, and it's linked right here.
